{{western name order|Sasada Makiko}}
'''Makiko Sasada''' ({{langx|ja|佐々田槙子}}) is a Japanese mathematician and mathematical physicist. Her research applies [[probability theory]] and [[statistical physics]] in understanding [[differential equation]]s such as the [[Navier–Stokes equations]] for fluid flow as the scaling limits of [[particle system]]s.{{r|utokyo}} She is also known for her web site encouraging Japanese girls in mathematics.{{r|aera}} She is a professor in the Graduate School of Mathematical Sciences at the [[University of Tokyo]].{{r|utokyo}}

==Education and career==
Sasada was born in the United States, circa 1985, but returned with her family to Japan as an infant. Her mother worked as a translator and her father as a research physicist.{{r|aera}} She completed her Ph.D. in 2011 at the University of Tokyo, with support as a research fellow of the [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]].{{r|researchmap}} Her doctoral work was jointly supervised by {{ill|Stefano Olla|de}} and {{ill|Tadahisa Funaki|ja|舟木直久}}.{{r|mg}}

She became an assistant professor at [[Keio University]] from 2011 to 2014, continuing there in 2014–2015 as a lecturer{{r|researchmap}} (senior assistant professor).{{r|ashida}} In 2015 she obtained an associate professor position at the University of Tokyo, where she was promoted to full professor in 2023. She added a second affiliation with the [[Riken]] Laboratory of Mathematics in 2017.{{r|researchmap}}

==Recognition==
Sasada received the Takebe Katahiro Prize for Encouragement of Young Researchers of the Mathematical Society of Japan in 2010, the University of Tokyo President's prize in 2011,{{r|utokyo}} and the JSPS Ikushi Prize of the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science in 2011.{{r|ikushi}} She was the 2021 recipient of the Jun Ashida Brilliant Female Researchers Award of the Japan Science and Technology Agency.{{r|ashida}} The National Institute of Science and Technology Policy (NISTEP) named her as an NISTEP Selection researcher in 2025.{{r|nistep}}

Sasada was listed in the 2022 [[Asian Scientist 100]].{{r|as}} She is an invited speaker at the 2026 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].{{r|icm}}

==Personal life==
Sasada married a banker in 2013. They have two children, the second one born in [[New York City]] during the [[COVID-19 lockdowns]].{{r|aera}}
